scenes.headline: How Google's ax keeps one writer per conversation
scenes.sub: The single writer, the event log and recovery, read from the code.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Lentil! Google's ax promises consistent agent state and automatic recovery. Here's how both actually work.

scenes.text: The unit of ownership is the conversation. The lock is a Go map inside one process, and the reference deployment runs three.
scenes.mark: a Go map inside one process
scenes.say: The unit of ownership is the conversation. The lock is a Go map inside one process, and the reference deployment runs three of them.

steps.say: A turn arrives. The server adds the conversation to an in-memory map, and refuses a second caller.
Each step is appended to a shared event log. When the call returns, the entry is deleted. No lease, no fencing.
But the map lives in one process. A second replica has its own empty map, and admits the same conversation.

steps.note: In the author's probe, one request produced ten output frames
steps.say: In the author's test, both replicas were admitted, and one ran the turn twice.

scenes.title: Where a resume repeats work
scenes.say: Replay reduces the log to two fields: the last state, and which harness ran. Nothing records which tools already ran.

items.text: Post the turn to the model

items.say: Run them. That's where the email gets sent.
Only then does the cursor move. Crash in between, and a resume runs the tools again.

scenes.label: irreversible actions, where six were asked for, after one interruption and one follow-up
scenes.note: the same turn ran three times
scenes.say: Measured: one interrupted turn plus one follow-up ran the same work three times, and took fourteen irreversible actions where six were asked for.

left.title: v0.2.3: a framework
items: Rewrite your agent as its gRPC service
Speak its own Step message types
An event log in Postgres or SQLite
left.say: Before, ax was a framework: you rewrote your agent as its service and spoke its message types.

right.title: v0.3.0: an orchestrator
items: Your agent is an opaque command in a container
right.say: In September it deleted all that. Now your agent is just a command in a container.

scenes.text: Making a decision cheap is a modelling problem. Making sure it's acted on only once is a systems problem.

recap: Ownership is per conversation, enforced per process
The log replays to two fields, not to state
Effects can repeat: 14 actions where 6 were asked
scenes.say: To recap: a per-process lock, a two-field replay, and effects that can repeat.
